title: Story: Jack and the Beanstalk
summary: Jack swaps the cow for magic beans; the beanstalk grows up to the sky and the giant's castle. Present tense, clauses with weil / als / bis and lots of separable verbs.
phrases: We have to sell the cow.
I'll give you something special for it.
He swaps the cow for the beans.
Something strange happens in the night. |
He takes as much gold as he can carry.
They are glad it's all over.
lines: Jack and the Beanstalk.
Jack lives with his mother in a small village.
They are very poor.
They have only one cow.
The cow gives them a little milk, but they don't earn enough money.
One day his mother says to Jack: "We have to sell the cow at the market."
Jack isn't happy, but he helps his mother.
The next morning Jack goes to the market with the cow.
He's a little sad because they have to sell the cow.
On the way he meets an old man.
The man looks at the cow and says: "Your cow is very beautiful.
I'll give you something special for it."
Jack asks curiously: "What?"
The old man shows him a small bundle of beans.
He says: "These are magic beans. They are very valuable."
Jack believes him and thinks the beans may be better than money.
So he swaps the cow for the beans.
When Jack comes home, his mother is very angry.
She shouts: "What have you done? These beans are worthless!"
Then she throws the beans out of the window.
Jack is sad and goes to bed.
In the night something strange happens.
The beans begin to grow in the garden.
They grow very fast and become a huge beanstalk.
It grows higher and higher until it reaches the sky.
The next morning Jack looks out of the window and sees the big beanstalk.
He is very surprised and curious.
He asks himself: "Where does this beanstalk lead?"
He thinks for a while.
Then he decides to explore the beanstalk.
He goes into the garden and touches the plant.
It is very thick and strong.
Slowly he begins to climb up it.
The beanstalk is very tall.
Jack climbs up for a long time.
Below him the house gets smaller and smaller.
At last the clouds are below him.
After a long time Jack reaches a place above the clouds.
There he sees something very unusual: a big castle.
He is amazed and stops for a moment.
The castle looks old and big.
He wonders: "Who might live here?"
Slowly he goes to the door and opens it quietly.
Jack is a little afraid, but his curiosity is stronger.
He steps into the castle.
It seems as if nobody is there.
Everything is very big and quiet.
The furniture is huge and the room seems strangely calm.
Jack slowly looks around and suddenly hears heavy footsteps.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The floor begins to shake.
He gets a fright and quickly hides behind a big cupboard.
A huge man comes into the room.
It's a giant.
He sits down at the table and eats a lot.
Then the giant takes out a big bag.
He puts it on the table and pours out lots of gold coins.
The giant looks at them contentedly.
Jack keeps very still and watches the giant from his hiding place.
He waits a long time until the giant is full and finally falls asleep.
The giant's breathing becomes slow and deep.
Now Jack moves very carefully.
He goes quietly to the table.
He takes as much gold as he can carry.
Then he goes slowly to the door.
When he is outside, he runs quickly to the beanstalk and starts climbing down.
After a while Jack is back home with his mother.
They are happy now because they have gold.
They buy food and live better than before.
But Jack still thinks about the big castle above the clouds.
Jack climbs up the beanstalk again.
In the castle he waits until the giant is asleep.
Then he goes quietly into the room and finds a golden goose.
This goose lays golden eggs every day.
He carefully takes it with him and goes quickly back home.
Jack and his mother become even richer.
Now they live very comfortably and have no more worries.
But Jack isn't satisfied.
He thinks: "There must be even more in the castle."
A third time Jack climbs up the beanstalk.
Again he goes into the castle.
This time he finds a special golden harp.
When he touches it, the harp starts to shout loudly: "Help! Help!"
The giant wakes up at once and gets very angry.
He realises that someone has been in his castle again.
The giant runs quickly out of the castle and sees Jack on the beanstalk.
Jack climbs down as fast as he can.
His heart is pounding because he is very scared.
The giant starts climbing down the beanstalk too.
The beanstalk sways hard under their weight.
Jack gets closer and closer to the ground.
He shouts loudly: "Mother, the axe, quick!"
His mother comes out of the house at once with an axe.
Jack reaches the ground, runs off and points at the beanstalk.
The giant is still up there and coming closer and closer.
His mother quickly strikes the beanstalk with the axe.
After a few blows the beanstalk slowly collapses.
The giant is still up there and loses his grip.
He falls into the depths and disappears.
Jack and his mother are safe now.
They are very glad that it's all over.
With the treasures from the castle they become rich.
And so Jack and his mother lived happily ever after.
topics: Retell the story: how does Jack get rich?
A swap: what would you swap, and for what?
Curiosity and courage: when were you brave?

focus.title: Subordinate clauses
points: weil (because): Er ist traurig, weil sie die Kuh verkaufen müssen. — verb at the end
als (when, once in the past / in a story): Als Jack nach Hause kommt, ist seine Mutter wütend.
bis (until): Er wartet, bis der Riese schläft.
If the clause comes first, the main verb follows straight after: Als er sie berührt, beginnt die Harfe …

focus.title: Separable verbs
points: hochklettern / hinaufklettern: Jack klettert die Bohnenranke hinauf.
einschlafen, aufwachen: Der Riese schläft ein · Er wacht sofort auf.
nachdenken: Er denkt eine Weile nach. · anfassen: Er fasst die Pflanze an.
With zu, zu goes in the middle: hochzuklettern · hinunterzuklettern

focus.title: Comparatives
points: -er: klein → kleiner · reich → reicher · hoch → höher
Some take an umlaut: stark → stärker · nah → näher
immer + comparative = more and more: immer kleiner · immer näher
als to compare: besser als Geld · besser als früher

focus.title: Something + adjective
points: After etwas the adjective gets a capital letter and -es: etwas Besonderes · etwas Seltsames
etwas sehr Ungewöhnliches = something very unusual
The same with nichts: nichts Neues = nothing new
With viel: viel Gutes = a lot of good

focus.title: Two-way prepositions
points: Place (Dativ): hinter einem Schrank · auf der Bohnenranke · über den Wolken
Direction (Akkusativ): in den Garten · auf den Tisch · in den Himmel
Question wo? → Dativ · question wohin? → Akkusativ
Er legt ihn auf den Tisch (wohin) ↔ Das Gold liegt auf dem Tisch (wo)
